Aalar

also Immer

McClintock & Strong, Cyclopaedia, vol. I, 1867

(Greek Aalar), a person who (or a place from which some of the Jews) returned after the captivity (1 Esdras v, 36); more correctly called in the parallel list (Neh. vii, 61) Immer (q.v.).

Editorial Note (Wroot Press, 2026): M&S leaves the person-or-place question open, but the parallel list in Ezra 2:59/Nehemiah 7:61 is a list of Babylonian locations that returning exiles could not trace their genealogy back to (Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer) — a place-name convention, not a list of ancestors. On that pattern Immer/Aalar is best read as a place, not a person, resolving the ambiguity M&S’s source (1 Esdras, a looser Greek paraphrase of Ezra-Nehemiah) left unclear.
